summary: Live dashboard aggregation window skew after upstream ingest throttle causing duplicate alert links
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NovaHealth) reported that live dashboards for several routes show a sudden duplication of alert links and inconsistent hourly aggregation counts starting ~2026-03-10T14:00Z. The skew correlates with a sustained ingest throttle event in the analytics pipeline that same hour.

Impact:
- Multiple alert cards show duplicate links to the same incident (same incident id shown twice) causing repeated escalation notifications to NovaHealth on Slack.
- Hourly rollups for usage and error-rate charts are missing 5-15 minute buckets and then show duplicate aggregated counts when the pipeline resumes (double-counting).
- Customer-facing dashboards and scheduled reports may include inflated totals for the affected hour.

Environment:
prod (us-east region). Customer org has high-cardinality route tagging and org-attribute sync enabled.

Observed behavior:
- Aggregation window alignment shifted: when ingest backpressure occurred, new events were queued then reingested with original timestamps, but aggregation job re-ran overlapping windows causing duplicates.
- Trace links inserted into alert payloads included a stale tracehook token and a fresh token, resulting in two alert links (stale -> 404 if used later).

Expected behavior:
- Aggregation engine should deduplicate overlapping reingests and respect a single canonical evaluation window per hourly rollup.
- Alert payloads should contain only active tracehook tokens and not carry forward expired/stale tokens.

Attachments/Logs:
- sample_query_id: 7f4c2b1a
- SLF4J snippets from aggregator and ingest: see logs below.

Temporary workaround recommended:
- For NovaHealth we've suppressed duplicate alert routing rule in their org settings to stop the noisy escalations while we investigate.
- We advised the customer to hold non-critical scheduled reports for the 14:00-15:00 window until a correction is applied.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Trigger ingest backpressure on a high-cardinality org by temporarily dropping downstream consumer (simulated in staging).
2) Allow events to buffer and then re-enable the consumer so backlog is reprocessed.
3) Observe hourly rollup job outputs for the window during which the backlog was reprocessed.
4) Observe alerts created for routes with tracehook tokens that were rotated during the backlog period.

comments: 2026-03-10 14:30 - NovaHealth (support@novahealth.com): We received three escalate notifications at 14:20 all pointing to the same incident. Looks like your console showed the alert twice.

2026-03-10 14:45 - Support (Priya Nair): Acknowledged. We've temporarily muted duplicate escalation routing for your org and opened this incident. Engineering is investigating ingestion and aggregation overlap. ETA for first update: 1 hour.

2026-03-10 15:20 - Eng (Evan Chen): Preliminary triage: ingest backlog replay caused aggregator to start a second overlapping rollup job. Hypothesis: scheduler doesn't check in-progress windows when backlog replay triggers immediate backfill. Adding reproducer in staging now.

2026-03-10 16:05 - Eng (Evan Chen): Replayed backlog in staging; confirmed duplicate windows and duplicate alert link insertion when tracehook rotation occurs mid-backfill. Recording reproducer and relevant logs in linked PR.

2026-03-12 09:10 - Support (Priya Nair): Customer confirmed suppression stopped noisy Slack pagers overnight. They requested a permanent fix and a post-incident correction for the affected report exports.
investigation_notes:
2026-03-10 15:00 - Investigation started.
2026-03-10 15:20 - Found two aggregator job invocations covering overlapping windows: job A (13:00-14:00) and job B (13:50-14:50). Job B started after backlog replay began.
2026-03-10 15:35 - Scheduler code path does not atomically mark windows 'in-progress' when a backlog-triggered rollup is scheduled; race allows a subsequent scheduler tick to schedule an overlapping run.
2026-03-10 16:00 - Alerting pipeline appended both stale and rotated tracehook tokens because token rotation ran between two alert assembly attempts for the same logical event.
2026-03-11 11:20 - Reproduced in staging with same org attribute settings and confirmed duplication of counts and duplicate alert links.
Action items captured: update scheduler to consult 'in-progress' index with stronger checks; dedupe ingested events for overlapping windows; ensure alert assembly is idempotent with respect to tracehook tokens.
resolution_notes:
Mitigation applied 2026-03-12 03:00: - Temporarily changed scheduler to avoid launching overlapping rollups during backlog drain (hotfix).
2026-03-12 04:45 - Backfill correction job ran to recompute affected hourly rollups for NovaHealth's org from 2026-03-10T13:00Z to 2026-03-10T15:00Z and replace duplicated aggregates.
2026-03-12 06:10 - Tracehook token assembly hardened: alert assembler now atomically fetches current token and discards stale tokens when assembling alert payloads.
Follow-ups: create PR to implement stronger 'in-progress' reservation in scheduler (linked PRs). Schedule a retro with ingest and aggregator owners. Notify customer when final verification is complete.
